To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most important factors to consider in the evaluation of alternative orbit spectrum regimes are (a) the costs of establishing a regime, (b) the costs of operating a regime, (c) the benefits of a regime, and (d) the costs of a regime to other regimes.

(a) the current orbit spectrum regime is a common pool regime that is not working; (b) the most promising alternative is a common pool, but with a limited number of users; (c) this regime would be improved by the addition of a property rights regime, but the latter would be costly to implement and would not be the most effective means of managing the orbit spectrum regime.

the optimal governance structure for the orbit spectrum resource is a hybrid regime in which the private sector and public sector share property rights and responsibilities, and that the optimal governance regime for the orbit spectrum is one that is based on the principles of the private property regime.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a set of policy issues associated with the management of a global common resource, the orbit spectrum resource, and the governance of the orbit spectrum resource regime.
the question of how to choose among the various proposals and regimes that are available for managing the orbit-spectrum resource.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no regime is better than any other.
there is not a single best regime for the orbit spectrum resource, and that the choice among alternative regimes depends on a number of factors.
there is no single best regime for the orbit spectrum commons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current regime is the best that could have been achieved given the political constraints of the time, but it is now time for an upgrade to a more efficient system.
the most important issue for space policy is not how to allocate the orbit spectrum resource, but how to allocate the costs of allocating it.
the most important factor in the management of orbit spectrum policy, as in other areas of global commons policy, is the establishment of property rights.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the orbit spectrum resource is best managed as a common resource with a global commons regime.
the choice of a governance structure should be based on the relative merits of the various structures, not on the merits of a particular regime.
a regime of property rights in outer space, if it were feasible, would not necessarily be superior to other regimes, including the status quo.
